claim: KPK cells had dramatically higher levels of Slc7a11 compared to KP controls.
source: Consistent with prior findings (Ishii et al., 1987; Lewerenz et al., 2013; Habib et al., 2015), gene expression analysis revealed dramatically higher levels of Slc7a11 in KPK cells compared to KP controls (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2B and citations to prior literature.

claim: The Nrf2-driven increase in expression of Slc7a11 and Gclc, and higher levels of GSH in KPK cells may result in export of glutamate in exchange for import of cystine.
source: We hypothesized that the Nrf2-driven increase in expression of Slc7a11 and Gclc, and higher levels of GSH in KPK cells may result in export of glutamate in exchange for import of cystine (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on inference from the observed increase in Slc7a11 and Gclc expression and GSH levels.

claim: Erastin treatment was sufficient to rescue the growth suppressive effects of glutamine deprivation in KPK cells with little effect on KP cells.
source: Indeed, Erastin treatment was sufficient to rescue the growth suppressive effects of both glutamine deprivation and CB-839 treatment in KPK cells with little effect on KP cells (Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Erastin treatment was sufficient to rescue the growth suppressive effects of CB-839 treatment in KPK cells with little effect on KP cells.
source: Indeed, Erastin treatment was sufficient to rescue the growth suppressive effects of both glutamine deprivation and CB-839 treatment in KPK cells with little effect on KP cells (Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: KEAP1 mutant human LUAD cell lines are robustly sensitive to glutaminase inhibition.
source: Furthermore, through the examination of a panel of human LUAD cell lines, we demonstrate that KEAP1 mutants are robustly sensitive to glutaminase inhibition (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Pre-treatment with Erastin overcomes sensitivity to glutaminase inhibition in KEAP1 mutant human LUAD lines.
source: Importantly, pre-treatment with Erastin overcomes sensitivity to glutaminase inhibition in KEAP1 mutant lines (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: xCT/Slc7a11 functions based on the intra- and extra- cellular gradients of cystine and glutamate in a concentration dependent manner.
source: xCT/Slc7a11 functions based on the intra- and extra- cellular gradients of cystine and glutamate in a concentration dependent manner (Briggs et al., 2016 Watanabe and Bannai, 1987).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Raising the levels of glutamate in the culture media rescued proliferation in KPK cells after CB-839 treatment.
source: By either raising the levels of glutamate or lowering the levels of cystine we were able to rescue proliferation in KPK cells after CB-839 treatment (Figure 2D and E).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Lowering the levels of cystine in the culture media rescued proliferation in KPK cells after CB-839 treatment.
source: By either raising the levels of glutamate or lowering the levels of cystine we were able to rescue proliferation in KPK cells after CB-839 treatment (Figure 2D and E).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Knockdown of Slc7a11 by two independent shRNAs rescued KPK cells from CB-839 treatment.
source: In line with expectations, knockdown of Slc7a11 by two independent shRNAs rescued KPK cells from both CB-839 treatment as well as glutamine deprivation while shCTRL had no effect (Figure 2F and Figure 2—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2F and Figure 2—figure supplement 2C.

claim: Knockdown of Slc7a11 by two independent shRNAs rescued KPK cells from glutamine deprivation.
source: In line with expectations, knockdown of Slc7a11 by two independent shRNAs rescued KPK cells from both CB-839 treatment as well as glutamine deprivation while shCTRL had no effect (Figure 2F and Figure 2—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2F and Figure 2—figure supplement 2C.

claim: Modulating the levels of glutamate or cystine in the media did not provide additional benefits to depletion of Slc7a11 in regards to sensitivity to CB-839.
source: In addition, modulating the levels of glutamate or cystine in the media did not provide additional benefits to depletion of Slc7a11 in regards to sensitivity to CB-839 or glutamine deprivation (Figure 2F and Figure 2—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2F and Figure 2—figure supplement 2C.

claim: Modulating the levels of glutamate or cystine in the media did not provide additional benefits to depletion of Slc7a11 in regards to sensitivity to glutamine deprivation.
source: In addition, modulating the levels of glutamate or cystine in the media did not provide additional benefits to depletion of Slc7a11 in regards to sensitivity to CB-839 or glutamine deprivation (Figure 2F and Figure 2—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2F and Figure 2—figure supplement 2C.

claim: Increased expression of xCT/Slc7a11 through Nrf2 hyperactivation in Keap1 mutant cells is necessary for the increased glutamine dependency and sensitivity to glutaminase inhibitors.
source: Taken together, these results indicate that increased expression of xCT/Slc7a11 through Nrf2 hyperactivation in Keap1 mutant cells is necessary for the increased glutamine dependency and sensitivity to glutaminase inhibitors.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data showing that Slc7a11 knockdown rescues sensitivity to CB-839 and glutamine deprivation.

claim: CB-839 treatment suppressed tumor growth only in KPK cells, but had no effect on KP tumors.
source: CB-839 treatment suppressed tumor growth only in KPK cells, but had no effect on KP tumors (Figure 2G and H and Figure 2—figure supplement 2D and E).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2G, 2H, and Figure 2—figure supplement 2D and E.

claim: Knockdown of Slc7a11 completely abrogated the effect of CB-839 on KPK tumors.
source: Knockdown of Slc7a11 completely abrogated the effect of CB-839 on KPK tumors (Figure 2H and Figure 2—figure supplement 2E).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2H and Figure 2—figure supplement 2E.

claim: Keap1 mutations result in a metabolic liability to glutaminase inhibition in vivo driven by increased expression of xCT/Slc7a11 in KPK cells.
source: These data strongly support the notion that Keap1 mutations result in a metabolic liability to glutaminase inhibition in vivo driven by increased expression of xCT/Slc7a11 in KPK cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the in vivo experimental data showing that Slc7a11 knockdown abrogates CB-839 sensitivity.

claim: Keap1 mutant cells are dependent on glutamine due to basally decreased intracellular pools of glutamate.
source: Keap1 mutant cells are dependent on glutamine due to basally decreased intracellular pools of glutamate, partially because of increased secretion via xCT and increased production of GSH.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data showing decreased intracellular glutamate and increased secretion.

claim: Decreased intracellular pools of glutamate in Keap1 mutant cells is partially because of increased secretion via xCT.
source: Keap1 mutant cells are dependent on glutamine due to basally decreased intracellular pools of glutamate, partially because of increased secretion via xCT and increased production of GSH.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data showing increased glutamate secretion and the role of xCT.

claim: Decreased intracellular pools of glutamate in Keap1 mutant cells is partially because of increased production of GSH.
source: Keap1 mutant cells are dependent on glutamine due to basally decreased intracellular pools of glutamate, partially because of increased secretion via xCT and increased production of GSH.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data showing increased GSH production.

claim: Glutamate can fuel GSH synthesis or be converted to α-KG via transamination.
source: Glutamate can fuel both GSH synthesis, or via transamination be converted to α-KG, a carbon source for the TCA cycle (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about glutamate metabolism.

claim: α-KG is a carbon source for the TCA cycle.
source: Glutamate can fuel both GSH synthesis, or via transamination be converted to α-KG, a carbon source for the TCA cycle (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about the TCA cycle.

claim: Supplementation with antioxidants trolox or N-acetyl cysteine did not rescue proliferation after glutamine deprivation in KPK cells.
source: However, supplementation with these antioxidants did not rescue proliferation after glutamine deprivation or glutaminase inhibition in KPK cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and Figure 3B).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and Figure 3B.

claim: Supplementation with antioxidants trolox or N-acetyl cysteine did not rescue proliferation after glutaminase inhibition in KPK cells.
source: However, supplementation with these antioxidants did not rescue proliferation after glutamine deprivation or glutaminase inhibition in KPK cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and Figure 3B).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and Figure 3B.

claim: High antioxidant production in KPK cells driven by Nrf2 activation increases cellular demand for glutamate.
source: We hypothesized that high antioxidant production in KPK cells driven by Nrf2 activation increases cellular demand for glutamate.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on inference from the observed metabolic phenotypes.

claim: Glutamate is required to synthesize glutathione while limiting availability for other cellular processes such as fueling the TCA cycle.
source: Glutamate is required in order to synthesize glutathione while limiting availability for other cellular processes such as fueling the TCA cycle.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data and inference about the metabolic trade-off.

claim: Pretreatment with dimethyl 2-oxoglutarate rescued sensitivity to CB-839 in KPK cells.
source: Consistent with this hypothesis, pretreatment with: (1) dimethyl 2-oxoglutarate (DMG), a cell permeable α-KG analogue, or (2) pyruvate, a glucose-derived TCA cycle carbon source, rescued sensitivity to CB-839 and glutamine deprivation in KPK cells (Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Pretreatment with pyruvate rescued sensitivity to CB-839 in KPK cells.
source: Consistent with this hypothesis, pretreatment with: (1) dimethyl 2-oxoglutarate (DMG), a cell permeable α-KG analogue, or (2) pyruvate, a glucose-derived TCA cycle carbon source, rescued sensitivity to CB-839 and glutamine deprivation in KPK cells (Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Pretreatment with dimethyl 2-oxoglutarate rescued sensitivity to glutamine deprivation in KPK cells.
source: Consistent with this hypothesis, pretreatment with: (1) dimethyl 2-oxoglutarate (DMG), a cell permeable α-KG analogue, or (2) pyruvate, a glucose-derived TCA cycle carbon source, rescued sensitivity to CB-839 and glutamine deprivation in KPK cells (Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Pretreatment with pyruvate rescued sensitivity to glutamine deprivation in KPK cells.
source: Consistent with this hypothesis, pretreatment with: (1) dimethyl 2-oxoglutarate (DMG), a cell permeable α-KG analogue, or (2) pyruvate, a glucose-derived TCA cycle carbon source, rescued sensitivity to CB-839 and glutamine deprivation in KPK cells (Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Sensitivity to glutaminase inhibition is due to decreased glutamate availability for anaplerosis or other biosynthetic reactions, not synthesis of the antioxidant GSH.
source: These results suggest that sensitivity to glutaminase inhibition is due to decreased glutamate availability for anaplerosis or other biosynthetic reactions, not synthesis of the antioxidant GSH.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data showing that antioxidants do not rescue but anaplerotic substrates do.

claim: Reducing GSH levels in KPK cells with L-Buthionine sulfoximine did not alter sensitivity to CB-839.
source: In line with this, reducing GSH levels in KPK cells with L-Buthionine sulfoximine (BSO) did not alter sensitivity to CB-839 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B and C).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B and C.

claim: Hyperactivation of Nrf2 by Keap1 mutation genetically reprograms cells to produce high levels of antioxidants at the expense of contributing carbon to replenish the TCA cycle.
source: Our data suggests that hyperactivation of Nrf2 by Keap1 mutation genetically reprograms cells to produce high levels of antioxidants at the expense of contributing carbon to replenish the TCA cycle.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data showing decreased TCA cycle metabolites and increased GSH.

claim: KPK cells have reduced total levels of TCA cycle intermediates.
source: Consistent with this data, KPK cells have reduced total levels of TCA cycle intermediates (Figure 3C) and supplementation with either 2 mM pyruvate or DMG increased total levels of TCA cycle intermediates in KPK cells equivalent to or in excess to those in KP cells (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Supplementation with 2 mM pyruvate or DMG increased total levels of TCA cycle intermediates in KPK cells equivalent to or in excess to those in KP cells.
source: Consistent with this data, KPK cells have reduced total levels of TCA cycle intermediates (Figure 3C) and supplementation with either 2 mM pyruvate or DMG increased total levels of TCA cycle intermediates in KPK cells equivalent to or in excess to those in KP cells (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: KPK cells incorporate less carbon from glutamine into the TCA cycle as compared to KP cells.
source: We observed that KPK cells incorporate less carbon from glutamine into the TCA cycle as compared to KP cells (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3E using stable isotope tracing.

claim: KPK cells have a basal deficiency in glutamine metabolism that contributes to their increased sensitivity to loss of glutamine-derived glutamate for anaplerosis.
source: Taken together, these data strongly suggest that KPK cells have a basal deficiency in glutamine metabolism that contributes to their increased sensitivity to loss of glutamine-derived glutamate for anaplerosis.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data showing decreased glutamine incorporation into TCA cycle and sensitivity to glutaminase inhibition.

claim: The TCA cycle generates NADH and FADH2 that will be used by the mitochondrial electron transport system to produce ATP.
source: A functional output of the TCA cycle is oxidative phosphorylation in the mitochondria, as the TCA cycle generates NADH and FADH2 that will be used by the mitochondrial electron transport system to produce ATP.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about the TCA cycle and oxidative phosphorylation.

claim: KPK cells have reduced oxygen consumption rates compared to KP cells indicating that Keap1 mutants have lower mitochondrial respiration basally.
source: Measuring mitochondrial respiration revealed that KPK cells have reduced oxygen consumption rates (OCR) compared to KP cells indicating that Keap1 mutants have lower mitochondrial respiration basally (Figure 3F).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3F.

claim: The overall decrease in respiration in KPK compared to KP cells is in line with decreased TCA cycle output.
source: The overall decrease in respiration in KPK compared to KP cells is in line with decreased TCA cycle output (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data showing both decreased TCA cycle metabolites and decreased OCR.

claim: Supplementation with pyruvate or DMG did not significantly increase basal OCR in KPK cells.
source: However, supplementation with pyruvate or DMG did not significantly increase basal OCR in KPK cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 3A).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3A.

claim: KPK cells have reduced reserve respiratory capacity as compared to KP cells.
source: This is likely a result of KPK cells having reduced reserve respiratory capacity as compared to KP cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 3B) in normal media conditions.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3B.

claim: CB-839 treatment reduced respiration in both KP and KPK cells.
source: As expected, CB-839 treatment reduced respiration in both KP and KPK cells, however, the drop in OCR after CB-839 administration was dramatically more pronounced in KPK cells (−50.8%) compared to KP cells (−21.6%), despite baseline levels being lower in KPK cells (Figure 3F and G).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3F and G.

claim: The drop in OCR after CB-839 administration was dramatically more pronounced in KPK cells (−50.8%) compared to KP cells (−21.6%).
source: As expected, CB-839 treatment reduced respiration in both KP and KPK cells, however, the drop in OCR after CB-839 administration was dramatically more pronounced in KPK cells (−50.8%) compared to KP cells (−21.6%), despite baseline levels being lower in KPK cells (Figure 3F and G).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3F and G.

claim: The drop in OCR in response to CB-839 was rescued by co-treatment with DMG or pyruvate.
source: The drop in OCR in response to CB-839 was rescued by co-treatment with DMG or pyruvate (Figure 3G).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3G.

claim: The ability of both DMG and pyruvate to rescue overall levels of TCA cycle metabolites as well as cellular proliferation and mitochondrial respiration in response to CB-839 treatment in KPK cells suggests that the basal defects in TCA cycle metabolism in KPK cells causes a metabolic bottleneck due to limited glutamate availability.
source: The ability of both DMG and pyruvate to rescue overall levels of TCA cycle metabolites as well as cellular proliferation and mitochondrial respiration in response to CB-839 treatment in KPK cells suggests that the basal defects in TCA cycle metabolism in KPK cells causes a metabolic bottleneck due to limited glutamate availability which is further exacerbated by glutaminase inhibition via CB-839.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data showing rescue by anaplerotic substrates.

claim: The basal defects in TCA cycle metabolism in KPK cells is further exacerbated by glutaminase inhibition via CB-839.
source: The ability of both DMG and pyruvate to rescue overall levels of TCA cycle metabolites as well as cellular proliferation and mitochondrial respiration in response to CB-839 treatment in KPK cells suggests that the basal defects in TCA cycle metabolism in KPK cells causes a metabolic bottleneck due to limited glutamate availability which is further exacerbated by glutaminase inhibition via CB-839.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data showing that CB-839 worsens the metabolic defects.

claim: Pyruvate carboxylase catalyzes the conversion of pyruvate to oxaloacetate.
source: One explanation is that pyruvate offers an alternative anaplerotic substrate via increased flux through pyruvate carboxylase, which catalyzes the conversion of pyruvate to oxaloacetate.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about pyruvate carboxylase.

claim: Treatment with CB-839 enhanced carbon flux through pyruvate carboxylase in normal media conditions.
source: In line with this hypothesis, we observed increased flux through pyruvate carboxylase in response to CB-839 in normal media conditions as well as when cells are supplemented with pyruvate (Figure 3I and J).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3I using stable isotope tracing.

claim: Treatment with CB-839 enhanced carbon flux through pyruvate carboxylase when cells are supplemented with pyruvate.
source: In line with this hypothesis, we observed increased flux through pyruvate carboxylase in response to CB-839 in normal media conditions as well as when cells are supplemented with pyruvate (Figure 3I and J).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3J using stable isotope tracing.

claim: KP tumors have increased PC flux.
source: This is in agreement with previous results indicating that KP tumors have increased PC flux (Davidson et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Keap1 mutations result in basal defects in central carbon metabolism, with KPK cells having overall decreased levels of TCA cycle intermediates.
source: Taken together these data show that Keap1 mutations result in basal defects in central carbon metabolism, with KPK cells having overall decreased levels of TCA cycle intermediates and reduced contribution of carbon from glutamine to these metabolites.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data showing decreased TCA cycle metabolites and reduced glutamine incorporation.

claim: Keap1 mutations result in reduced contribution of carbon from glutamine to TCA cycle metabolites.
source: Taken together these data show that Keap1 mutations result in basal defects in central carbon metabolism, with KPK cells having overall decreased levels of TCA cycle intermediates and reduced contribution of carbon from glutamine to these metabolites.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data showing reduced glutamine incorporation into TCA cycle.

claim: The metabolic imbalance in KPK cells can be therapeutically exploited by the use of glutaminase inhibitors to further limit glutamate availability.
source: This metabolic imbalance in KPK cells can be therapeutically exploited by the use of glutaminase inhibitors to further limit glutamate availability.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data showing sensitivity to glutaminase inhibition.

claim: Pretreatment with KI696 and subsequent Nrf2 activation was sufficient to induce strong growth suppression in response to CB-839 treatment in KP cells.
source: Pretreatment with KI696 and subsequent Nrf2 activation was sufficient to induce strong growth suppression in response to CB-839 treatment in KP cells (Figure 4B), similar to what we observed in KPK cells (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Effects of CB-839 in KI696-treated KP cells were rescued by pretreatment of anaplerotic precursors, pyruvate and DMG.
source: Additionally, effects of CB-839 were rescued both by pretreatment of anaplerotic precursors, pyruvate and DMG, and by modulating extracellular glutamate and cystine concentrations, but not by the antioxidants NAC and trolox (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Effects of CB-839 in KI696-treated KP cells were rescued by modulating extracellular glutamate and cystine concentrations.
source: Additionally, effects of CB-839 were rescued both by pretreatment of anaplerotic precursors, pyruvate and DMG, and by modulating extracellular glutamate and cystine concentrations, but not by the antioxidants NAC and trolox (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Effects of CB-839 in KI696-treated KP cells were not rescued by the antioxidants NAC and trolox.
source: Additionally, effects of CB-839 were rescued both by pretreatment of anaplerotic precursors, pyruvate and DMG, and by modulating extracellular glutamate and cystine concentrations, but not by the antioxidants NAC and trolox (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Increased sensitivity to CB-839 was only observed in KP cells that had increased expression of Slc7a11 in combination with either Gclc or Gclm.
source: However, we only observed increased sensitivity to CB-839 in KP cells that had increased expression of Slc7a11 in combination with either Gclc or Gclm (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Human KEAP1 wild type lung cancer cells, H2009, responded to KI696 with nuclear accumulation of NRF2.
source: Similar to mouse KP cells, human KEAP1 wild type lung cancer cells, H2009, responded to KI696 with nuclear accumulation of NRF2 and subsequent up regulation of target gene expression and total GSH levels (Figure 4E and Figure 4—figure supplement 2A–C).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Human KEAP1 wild type lung cancer cells, H2009, responded to KI696 with subsequent up regulation of target gene expression.
source: Similar to mouse KP cells, human KEAP1 wild type lung cancer cells, H2009, responded to KI696 with nuclear accumulation of NRF2 and subsequent up regulation of target gene expression and total GSH levels (Figure 4E and Figure 4—figure supplement 2A–C).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2A–C.

claim: Human KEAP1 wild type lung cancer cells, H2009, responded to KI696 with increased total GSH levels.
source: Similar to mouse KP cells, human KEAP1 wild type lung cancer cells, H2009, responded to KI696 with nuclear accumulation of NRF2 and subsequent up regulation of target gene expression and total GSH levels (Figure 4E and Figure 4—figure supplement 2A–C).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2A–C.

claim: Human H2009 cells responded strongly to co-treatment with CB-839 and KI696.
source: In line with KP cells, human H2009 cells responded strongly to co-treatment with CB-839 and KI696 and this synergistic effect was rescued by pretreatment of anaplerotic precursors, modulating extracellular glutamate and cystine concentrations but not by antioxidants (Figure 4F).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: The synergistic effect of CB-839 and KI696 in H2009 cells was rescued by pretreatment of anaplerotic precursors.
source: In line with KP cells, human H2009 cells responded strongly to co-treatment with CB-839 and KI696 and this synergistic effect was rescued by pretreatment of anaplerotic precursors, modulating extracellular glutamate and cystine concentrations but not by antioxidants (Figure 4F).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: The synergistic effect of CB-839 and KI696 in H2009 cells was rescued by modulating extracellular glutamate and cystine concentrations.
source: In line with KP cells, human H2009 cells responded strongly to co-treatment with CB-839 and KI696 and this synergistic effect was rescued by pretreatment of anaplerotic precursors, modulating extracellular glutamate and cystine concentrations but not by antioxidants (Figure 4F).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: The synergistic effect of CB-839 and KI696 in H2009 cells was not rescued by antioxidants.
source: In line with KP cells, human H2009 cells responded strongly to co-treatment with CB-839 and KI696 and this synergistic effect was rescued by pretreatment of anaplerotic precursors, modulating extracellular glutamate and cystine concentrations but not by antioxidants (Figure 4F).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: KP cells treated with KI696 had reduced total levels of TCA cycle intermediates, equivalent to that observed in KPK cells.
source: KP cells treated with KI696 had reduced total levels of TCA cycle intermediates (Figure 4G), equivalent to that observed in KPK cells (Figure 4G and Figure 3C).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4G and Figure 3C.

claim: Overall mitochondrial respiration was reduced upon treatment of wild type KP cells with KI696.
source: Additionally, overall mitochondrial respiration was reduced upon treatment of wild type KP cells with KI696, and further reduced by the addition of CB-839 (Figure 4H).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4H.

claim: Overall mitochondrial respiration in KI696-treated KP cells was further reduced by the addition of CB-839.
source: Additionally, overall mitochondrial respiration was reduced upon treatment of wild type KP cells with KI696, and further reduced by the addition of CB-839 (Figure 4H).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4H.

claim: Nrf2 activation is sufficient to rewire cellular metabolism, resulting in increased glutamine dependency and sensitivity to CB-839 treatment in both mouse and human LUAD lines.
source: These data demonstrate that Nrf2 activation is sufficient to rewire cellular metabolism, resulting in increased glutamine dependency and sensitivity to CB-839 treatment in both mouse and human LUAD lines.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data showing that KI696 treatment recapitulates the metabolic phenotype and CB-839 sensitivity of KEAP1 mutant cells.

claim: KEAP1/NRF2 mutations are found in cancers other than LUAD.
source: In addition to LUAD, KEAP1/NRF2 mutations are found in other cancers (Shibata et al., 2008a; Kim et al., 2010; Konstantinopoulos et al., 2011; Muscarella et al., 2011; Cancer Genome Atlas Research Network, 2014; Hanada et al., 2012; Jaramillo and Zhang, 2013; Sato et al., 2013; Goldstein et al., 2016; Fabrizio et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: For each cancer type tested, mutations in KEAP1 predicted sensitivity to CB-839.
source: For each cancer type, mutations in KEAP1 predicted sensitivity to CB-839 (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Co-treatment with KI696 was able to sensitize KEAP1 wild type cancer cells that were relatively insensitive to CB-839.
source: Importantly, co-treatment with KI696 was able to sensitize KEAP1 wild type cancer cells that were relatively insensitive to CB-839 (Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Glutaminase is an attractive target in lung adenocarcinoma in which the KEAP1/NRF2 axis is mutated.
source: Taken together, our data suggests that glutaminase is an attractive target in both lung adenocarcinoma and in other cancers in which the KEAP1/NRF2 axis is mutated and the glutaminase inhibitor CB-839 could be an effective therapeutic agent in patients with these genetic subtypes of cancer.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data showing sensitivity to CB-839 in KEAP1 mutant cells.

claim: Glutaminase is an attractive target in cancers other than lung adenocarcinoma in which the KEAP1/NRF2 axis is mutated.
source: Taken together, our data suggests that glutaminase is an attractive target in both lung adenocarcinoma and in other cancers in which the KEAP1/NRF2 axis is mutated and the glutaminase inhibitor CB-839 could be an effective therapeutic agent in patients with these genetic subtypes of cancer.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data showing sensitivity to CB-839 in KEAP1 mutant cells across multiple cancer types.

claim: The glutaminase inhibitor CB-839 could be an effective therapeutic agent in patients with KEAP1/NRF2 mutant cancers.
source: Taken together, our data suggests that glutaminase is an attractive target in both lung adenocarcinoma and in other cancers in which the KEAP1/NRF2 axis is mutated and the glutaminase inhibitor CB-839 could be an effective therapeutic agent in patients with these genetic subtypes of cancer.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data showing sensitivity to CB-839 in KEAP1 mutant cells and is presented as a suggestion.

claim: Glutaminase inhibition could be more broadly applicable in a variety of cancer types when combined with a small molecule activator of NRF2.
source: Additionally, glutaminase inhibition could be more broadly applicable in a variety of cancer types when combined with a small molecule activator of NRF2, which renders KEAP1 wild type cells highly sensitive to glutaminase inhibition.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data showing that KI696 sensitizes KEAP1 wild type cells to CB-839.

claim: A small molecule activator of NRF2 renders KEAP1 wild type cells highly sensitive to glutaminase inhibition.
source: Additionally, glutaminase inhibition could be more broadly applicable in a variety of cancer types when combined with a small molecule activator of NRF2, which renders KEAP1 wild type cells highly sensitive to glutaminase inhibition.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing that KI696 sensitizes KEAP1 wild type cells to CB-839.

claim: Tumorigenesis requires cancer cells to increase their metabolic output to support tumor growth.
source: Tumorigenesis requires cancer cells to increase their metabolic output to support tumor growth.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about cancer metabolism.

claim: Higher metabolic activity increases oxidative stress in the form of ROS, which can lead to oxidative damage of macromolecules.
source: Higher metabolic activity increases oxidative stress in the form of ROS, which can lead to oxidative damage of macromolecules.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about ROS and oxidative damage.

claim: Under physiologic conditions of increased ROS, the NRF2 stress response promotes an antioxidant network that will scavenge and clear ROS.
source: Under physiologic conditions of increased ROS, the NRF2 stress response promotes an antioxidant network that will scavenge and clear ROS.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about the NRF2 pathway.

claim: After ROS clearance NRF2 will once again be degraded through its interaction with KEAP1 and CUL3-mediated ubiquitination.
source: After ROS clearance NRF2 will once again be degraded through its interaction with KEAP1 and CUL3-mediated ubiquitination.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about the NRF2 pathway.

claim: NRF2 activation leads to changes in cellular metabolism to support increased synthesis of antioxidants.
source: NRF2 activation subsequently leads to changes in cellular metabolism to support increased synthesis of antioxidants (Mitsuishi et al., 2012; DeNicola et al., 2015), which have recently been shown to promote tumorigenesis (Romero et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Increased synthesis of antioxidants has been shown to promote tumorigenesis.
